messages:
anya: seeing a sudden latency and 5xx spike for model:redwood-micro-13b on us-west-2. dashboard shows token latency jumping from 45ms -> 250ms around 11:03 UTC. rolling deploy?
marcus: i see that. correlated with a huge drop in KV prefix hit rate — went from ~92% to ~11% in 2m. backend CPU for cache-proxy spiked.
runtime-bot: [ALERT] kv-prefix-service high-latency: p95=480ms, errors=12/min, node-count=6 -> 4, 11:04:12 UTC
leo: any recent changes to prompt normalization or tokenizer packs? those usually blow up cache keys.
sophia: pushed a tokenizer tweak at 10:58 (commit 7ab3d1f) that normalizes smart quotes and collapses repeated spaces. intended to fix prompt canonicalization for mirror tests.
marcus: that matches timeline. looking at key histograms now. before: top 1000 keys ~70% of traffic. after: key cardinality exploded (unique keys +12x).
anya: sample of mismatched keys: used to be: `~PREFIX|user_prompt_trimmed` now we have micro-variations with trailing nbsp and different unicode quotes.
leo: ok that explains miss surge. but why did cache-proxy CPU spike so high? miss storms should go to backend but our continuous batching should still smooth kernels.
marcus: profiling traces attached (abbrev):
```
PROFILE 11:05: kernel_selector: model=redwood-micro-13b seq_len=64 chosen_kernel=fast-attn-v2 fallback_kernel=attn-slow (coldstart 340ms)
BATCHER: concurrent_batches=14 avg_batch_size=1.8 (target 8)
KV_CLIENT: miss_rate=0.89 req_rate=1.2k/s backend_rps=1100 err_rate=0.9%
CACHE_PROXY: p95_read=420ms p99=1.2s qps=1.2k concurrency=48
```
marcus: kernel selection got worse because batcher shrank batch sizes to <2, so fast-attn-v2 selection logic decided it couldn't use optimized kernel due to padding overhead; we fell back to slower kernel raising token cost.
sophia: so two compounding problems: tokenizer change => cache key fragmentation => miss surge => lower batch packing => worse kernel selection => higher latency.
anya: we should emergency-disable prefix caching for redwood-micro-13b to reduce backend pressure and force consistent kernel behavior while we revert or patch keying.
leo: wdyt about disabling only prefix-level caching (keep per-request L1) and rate-limit cache-proxy to 600qps? that buys time.
marcus: oncall is ok with targeted disable. i'll patch rollout config now: `enable_prefix_cache=false` for model:redwood-micro-13b in us-west-2.
oncall: patch applied at 11:12 UTC. monitoring: cache-proxy qps dropped 43%, backend error rate fell to 0.2% and p95 token latency -> 70ms within 3 minutes.
anya: creating hotfix PR to revert the tokenizer normalization -> reintroduce safe-canonicalize that preserves NBSP and quote variants; also add a deterministic unicode-normalize step with hash-salt. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/commit/7ab3d1f-revert-hotfix
marcus: added a short-term mitigation in cache keyer: normalize multiple-space collapse only inside placeholder params, not across whole prompt. will ship as 11:40 UTC patch.
sophia: we should also add a warmup job for top-200 prompt templates after deploys. idea: on rollout, async prefetcher will prime KV with top templates and warm KV-client local caches.
leo: agree. we should also adjust batching heuristic: don't reduce target batch size below 4 unless measured 1s of sustained low QPS. that avoids kernel fallback on transient miss storms.
anya: action items: 1) revert tokenizer change (PR filed) 2) patch cache keyer (marcus) 3) deploy warmup prefetcher for top-200 templates (sophia) 4) adjust batcher heuristic threshold to min_batch=4 (leo) 5) incident writeup and next steps (anya).
marcus: i captured profiling artifacts and key histograms in the incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/1947654321-kv-warmup-debug/
sophia: QA note: add synthetic test that mutates unicode spaces/quotes and verifies identical final cache keys for canonical templates.
leo: follow-up: we should add telemetry: `cache_key_entropy` metric per model+region and alert if entropy jumps >3x in 5m.
oncall: marking incident resolved: cache-config rollback and limiter applied, latency and errors back to baseline at 11:17 UTC. will keep increased monitoring for 12h.
anya: thanks all. posting a short post-incident summary in #incidents and will link to this thread + artifacts. final root cause: tokenizer normalization introduced invisible-char changes that increased key cardinality, causing miss surge and cascading perf regressions affecting batching/kernel selection.
marcus: timeline + commit refs added to incident doc. recommend we schedule a deeper perf retro next week (include infra, serving, tokenizer owners).
sophia: adding retro invite. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
